items.meta_title: VPN for Apple TV and Android TV, Set Up From Your Phone | VpnHood!
items.meta_description: VpnHood! runs on Apple TV and Android TV with a screen made for the remote. Sign in and change settings from your phone with Remote Access.
items.title: On your TV
items.lead: Runs on Apple TV and Android TV, with a screen made for the remote. Your phone does the typing.
items.shot_alt: VpnHood! CONNECT's home screen on a TV, connected, with its Location, Split Countries, Protocol and Settings rows
items.platforms: Apple TV with tvOS 17.0 and later, and Android TV with Android 7.0 and later.
items.remote_desc: A remote is good for pressing Connect, not for typing. So the TV shows only what a remote can do: connect, the location, the countries to keep out of the VPN and the protocol. Anything that needs typing, such as signing in or changing a setting, opens Remote Access on the TV. Scan its code, and your phone's browser opens the app's own pages; every change you make there lands on the TV at once.
items.remote_alt: The Remote Access screen on a TV, with a code to scan and the address under it
items.how_desc: Remote Access works inside your own network, only while its screen is open on the TV, and only for a device that scanned its code. Nothing is installed on the phone: any browser will do, and so will a computer.
items.when_desc: When you want the TV's own apps to go through the VPN. A VPN on your phone does not cover the TV, even on the same Wi-Fi.
items.cost_desc: The phone must be on the same network as the TV while you make changes, and the link between them is not encrypted, so make them on a network you trust.
items.start_install: Install the app from the App Store on an Apple TV, or from Google Play on an Android TV.
items.start_phone: To sign in or change a setting, follow the TV: it shows a code to scan with your phone.
items.start_client: Using VpnHood! CLIENT? It connects with an access key, which you add from your phone: see how.
